title: Indonesia Inter-Island EV Ferry Guide
excerpt: Complete guide to inter-island EV travel in Indonesia via RORO ferries. Java to Bali (Ketapang→Gilimanuk), Java to Sumatra (Merak→Bakauheni), and Bali to Lombok (Padangbai→Lembar) routes. Charging at terminals, battery strategy, and sample itineraries for EV road trips across Indonesia's islands.
author: EV Charging Asia Team
content:
Indonesia Inter-Island EV Ferry Guide: Taking Your EV Across the Archipelago via RORO [2026]

Indonesia is the world's largest archipelago — 17,000+ islands stretching 5,000 km from Sabang to Merauke. For EV drivers, this presents a unique challenge and an incredible opportunity. The backbone of inter-island vehicle travel is the RORO (Roll-On/Roll-Off) ferry network, operated primarily by ASDP Indonesia Ferry (state-owned) and private operators like Kaizen Ferry.

In 2026, Indonesia's EV ecosystem is maturing fast. PLN (Perusahaan Listrik Negara) has deployed 700+ SPKLU charging stations across Java, Bali, Sumatra, and Lombok, and the Trans-Java Toll Road is now bookended by charging at both ends. The RORO ferries that connect Indonesia's major islands are increasingly EV-friendly — they accept electric vehicles at standard rates, and the terminals on both sides are gaining charging infrastructure.

This guide covers the three most important inter-island RORO routes for EV drivers, the charging infrastructure at every terminal, battery management strategy for sea crossings, and complete itineraries to help you plan your Indonesian island-hopping EV adventure.

How RORO Ferries Work for EVs in Indonesia

RORO (Roll-On/Roll-Off) ferries operate with a simple premise: you drive your vehicle onto the ferry, the crew secures it on the vehicle deck, and you ride as a passenger during the crossing. For EV drivers, the process is nearly identical to petrol cars — with a few EV-specific considerations.

  • ASDP and Kaizen Ferry both accept EVs at standard vehicle rates
  • Booking is recommended — use the ASDP Ferry app or Kaizen Ferry app for advance tickets
  • No formal SOC restrictions — but keeping under 80% is prudent for sea crossings
  • Documentation required: STNK (vehicle registration), SIM (driver's license), booking confirmation
  • Vehicle dimensions matter — standard EVs (Tesla Model Y, BYD Atto 3, Hyundai Ioniq 5, Wuling Air EV) fit easily; oversized vehicles need special arrangements
  • Cost: Vehicle fares range from Rp 150,000 to Rp 1,800,000 depending on route and vehicle class

EV Battery Strategy for RORO Ferries

Crossing Duration Recommended SOC Before Boarding Expected SOC After Crossing Strategy
30-60 min (Ketapang→Gilimanuk) 65-75% 60-70% Minimal drain — charge at departure terminal
1-2 hours (Merak→Bakauheni) 70-75% 55-65% Moderate drain — disable Sentry/dashcam
3-4 hours (Padangbai→Lembar) 70-75% 50-60% Significant drain — pre-charge fully before arrival

Key EV tips for Indonesian ferries:

  • Turn off Sentry Mode / Dashcam recording — saves 5-8% battery over longer crossings
  • Enable Transport Mode if your EV has it — prevents alarm triggers from the rocking motion
  • Crack windows slightly open (1-2 cm) — vehicle decks can reach 35-40°C
  • Keep charging cable accessible — in the boot, not the frunk — you'll need it on the other side
  • Download PLN Mobile app — required to activate SPKLU chargers across Indonesia
  • Download offline maps for the destination island — cell signal is patchy at sea

Route 1: Java → Bali (Ketapang → Gilimanuk) — The Most Popular Crossing

The Ketapang–Gilimanuk ferry is the busiest vehicle ferry in Indonesia, connecting Java's east coast (Banyuwangi) with Bali's west coast. It's the primary gateway for all vehicle traffic heading to Bali and sees hundreds of crossings daily.

Detail Information
Route Ketapang (Banyuwangi, Java) → Gilimanuk (Bali)
Ferry type RORO (ASDP Indonesia Ferry)
Distance (sea) ~3 km across the Bali Strait
Crossing time 30-60 minutes
Vehicle fare (one way) Rp 150,000-350,000 (~$10-22 USD)
Frequency Every 15-30 minutes (24 hours a day)
Operator ASDP Indonesia Ferry

This crossing is the shortest and most frequent of the major RORO routes. Ferries run around the clock, every 15-30 minutes, making it the most forgiving option for first-time EV ferry travellers.

Charging at Ketapang Terminal (Java Side)

Charger Type Power Location Notes
PLN SPKLU Ketapang Terminal DC Fast 50 kW Inside ferry terminal area Directly at terminal — charge while waiting
PLN SPKLU Banyuwangi City DC Fast 50 kW Banyuwangi town centre (3 km) Back-up option near restaurants
Hotel AC Charging (Banyuwangi) AC 7-22 kW Various hotels (Ketapang Indah, Aston Banyuwangi) Good for overnight pre-ferry stay

Charging at Gilimanuk Terminal (Bali Side)

Charger Type Power Location Notes
PLN SPKLU Gilimanuk DC Fast 50 kW Gilimanuk port area New as of early 2026 — 2x 50 kW units
PLN SPKLU Negara DC Fast 50 kW Negara town (15 km east) Alternative if port charger is busy
PLN SPKLU Cekik DC Fast 50 kW Cekik (8 km east) Midway between Gilimanuk and Negara

Note: The Gilimanuk SPKLU was installed in early 2026 as part of PLN's Bali charging expansion. Previously, the nearest DC charging was 20 km east in Negara. This is a game-changer for EV arrivals on Bali — you can now charge immediately after disembarking.

Charging Strategy: Java → Bali

Direction Strategy
From Surabaya/Malang Charge to 80% at Surabaya or Probolinggo. The drive to Ketapang (200-250 km) uses 40-50%. Charge at PLN SPKLU Ketapang to 70% while waiting for the ferry (15-20 min on 50 kW).
From Bali → Java (return) Charge at PLN SPKLU Gilimanuk (new, 50 kW) to 70% before boarding. Arrive Ketapang with ~65%. Drive east to Banyuwangi or Probolinggo for next charge.
From South Bali → Gilimanuk Charge to 80% in Denpasar or Gianyar before the 3-hour drive west across Bali (Kuta→Gilimanuk: ~120 km). Gilimanuk has charging on arrival.

Route 2: Java → Sumatra (Merak → Bakauheni) — The Longest Crossing

The Merak–Bakauheni ferry is the primary vehicle link between Java and Sumatra, crossing the Sunda Strait. It's the longest of Indonesia's major RORO crossings and the most critical for anyone looking to drive their EV from Jakarta to Lampung, Palembang, or beyond.

Detail Information
Route Merak (Banten, Java) → Bakauheni (Lampung, Sumatra)
Ferry type RORO (ASDP Indonesia Ferry)
Distance (sea) ~30 km across the Sunda Strait
Crossing time 1-2 hours
Vehicle fare (one way) Rp 300,000-800,000 (~$19-50 USD)
Frequency Every 30-60 minutes (24 hours a day)
Operator ASDP Indonesia Ferry

This crossing is the busiest and most strategically important ferry route in Indonesia. It connects the Trans-Java Toll Road with the Trans-Sumatra Toll Road, making it a critical link for anyone driving the full length of Indonesia's two largest islands.

Charging at Merak Terminal (Java Side)

Charger Type Power Location Notes
PLN SPKLU Merak (Terminal) DC Fast 50 kW Inside Merak ferry complex 2x 50 kW CCS2 units — charge while queuing
PLN SPKLU Merak (AC) AC 7-22 kW Merak ferry complex 4x AC chargers — slower but good for full charge overnight
PLN SPKLU Cilegon DC Fast 50 kW Cilegon city (5 km from Merak) Alternative if terminal chargers are full
PLN SPKLU Serang DC Fast 50 kW Serang (20 km east) Last-chance charger on the Jakarta-Merak highway

Charging at Bakauheni Terminal (Sumatra Side)

Charger Type Power Location Notes
PLN SPKLU Bakauheni (Terminal) DC Fast 50 kW Inside Bakauheni ferry complex 3x 50 kW CCS2 units — arrive and charge immediately
PLN SPKLU Bakauheni (SPKLU Hub) DC Fast 50 kW Bakauheni port area Additional SPKLU units, part of PLN's Trans-Sumatra expansion
PLN SPKLU Kalianda DC Fast 50 kW Kalianda (15 km north on Trans-Sumatra) First stop on the Trans-Sumatra Toll Road
PLN SPKLU Bandar Lampung DC Fast 50-100 kW Bandar Lampung city (85 km north) Multiple SPKLU units including newer 100 kW units

Charging Strategy: Java → Sumatra

Direction Strategy
From Jakarta → Merak Charge to 70-75% at PLN SPKLU in Tangerang, Serang, or Cilegon. The drive from central Jakarta to Merak is ~100 km (1.5-2 hours). Arrive Merak with 55-60%. Top up at Merak terminal SPKLU (50 kW, 20 min) to 70% before boarding.
Bakauheni arrival Upon disembarking in Sumatra, drive directly to the PLN SPKLU inside the terminal (3x 50 kW units). Charge to 80% — this is your only safe charging point for the next 85 km to Bandar Lampung.
From Sumatra → Java (return) Charge to 70% at Bakauheni terminal before boarding. The 1-2 hour crossing will drain 5-10%. Arrive Merak with ~55-60%. Top up at Merak terminal SPKLU before driving to Jakarta.

Route 3: Bali → Lombok (Padangbai → Lembar) — The Emerging Route

The Padangbai–Lembar ferry is the third major RORO route, connecting Bali to Lombok across the Lombok Strait. This route has seen significant improvements in 2026 with expanded charging on both sides.

Detail Information
Route Padangbai (East Bali) → Lembar (Southwest Lombok)
Ferry type RORO (ASDP Indonesia Ferry)
Distance (sea) ~38 km across the Lombok Strait
Crossing time 3-4 hours
Vehicle fare (one way) Rp 250,000-400,000 (~$16-25 USD)
Frequency 8-12 departures daily (6 AM – 8 PM)
Operator ASDP Indonesia Ferry

This crossing is longer and less frequent than the Java-Bali or Java-Sumatra routes, but it's the gateway to Lombok, Mandalika, and the Gili Islands. For a detailed breakdown of this route, see our dedicated Bali to Lombok EV Ferry Guide.

Charging Near Padangbai (Bali Side)

Charger Type Power Distance to Padangbai Notes
PLN SPKLU Amankila DC Fast 60 kW 20 km north (30 min) Closest DC to Padangbai, resort setting
PLN SPKLU Candidasa DC Fast 50 kW 25 km north (35 min) Easy access from coastal road
ChargeIN Gianyar Supercharger Hub DC Fast 120 kW 35 km west (50 min) Fastest charger in east Bali
PLN SPKLU Sanur DC Fast 60 kW 55 km west (1 hr 15 min) Good stop if coming from south Bali

Charging on Lombok (Arrival Side)

Charger Type Power Distance to Lembar Notes
PLN SPKLU Mataram (Ampenan) DC Fast 50 kW 30 km north (40 min) Immediate post-ferry stop
PLN SPKLU Mandalika (Grid Pertamina) DC Fast 60 kW 50 km southeast (1 hr) Best DC on Lombok
PLN SPKLU Senggigi DC Fast 50 kW 45 km northwest (1 hr) Tourist strip charging
Hotel AC charging AC 7-22 kW Across Mataram, Senggigi, Mandalika Use as overnight backup

Charging Infrastructure at Indonesian Ferry Terminals — Summary

Terminal Island DC Fast Charging AC Charging Status (June 2026)
Ketapang Java (east) 1x 50 kW SPKLU Nearby hotels (7 kW) ✅ Operational
Gilimanuk Bali (west) 2x 50 kW SPKLU (NEW) — ✅ New — installed early 2026
Merak Java (west) 2x 50 kW CCS2 4x AC units ✅ Operational
Bakauheni Sumatra (south) 3x 50 kW CCS2 + SPKLU — ✅ Operational
Padangbai Bali (east) — (nearest: Amankila, 20 km) — ⚠️ No on-terminal charging
Lembar Lombok (southwest) — (nearest: Mataram, 30 km) — ⚠️ No on-terminal charging

What to Bring for an Inter-Island EV Ferry Trip

  • Type 2 charging cable (Mode 3) — essential for hotel AC charging on all islands
  • CCS2 adapter — not typically needed (Indonesia is CCS2-native), but carry a CHAdeMO adapter if your EV supports it for older stations
  • Granny charger (portable EVSE) — your emergency backup. A standard 220V Indonesian wall outlet adds 10-12 km/hour. Even a few hours of granny charging at a homestay or terminal office can save your trip
  • PLN Mobile app — installed and registered before departure. Add GoPay, OVO, or QRIS payment method. Some SPKLU stations require an Indonesian phone number
  • ChargeIN app — good backup for Bali and some Java chargers
  • Vehicle registration (STNK) — required for ferry check-in
  • Offline Google Maps — download maps for Java, Bali, Sumatra, and Lombok before you go
  • Join the "EV Indonesia" Telegram group — real-time charger status updates from local EV drivers

Sample Itineraries

Itinerary 1: 3-Day Java Explorer (Jakarta → Merak → Bakauheni → Bandar Lampung)

A quick weekend trip from Jakarta into Sumatra — perfect for testing the Merak–Bakauheni crossing.

Day Route Activities Charging Plan
Day 1 Jakarta → Merak (100 km, 2 hrs) Drive to Merak, afternoon ferry to Bakauheni (1-2 hrs), drive to Bandar Lampung (85 km, 1.5 hrs) Charge to 75% at PLN SPKLU Tangerang or Serang before Merak. Arrive Merak ~55%. Top up at Merak terminal SPKLU (50 kW, 20 min) to 70%. Board ferry. Arrive Bakauheni ~55%. Charge at Bakauheni terminal SPKLU (3x 50 kW) to 80%. Drive to Bandar Lampung.
Day 2 Bandar Lampung exploration Lampung Museum, Emplas Coffee plantation, Teluk Kiluan dolphin watching Charge at PLN SPKLU Bandar Lampung (50-100 kW, 30 min) while having lunch. Resort AC charging overnight.
Day 3 Bandar Lampung → Bakauheni → Merak → Jakarta Morning drive back to Bakauheni (85 km). Ferry to Merak. Drive to Jakarta (100 km). Charge to 70% in Bandar Lampung before departure. Arrive Bakauheni ~55%. Charge at Bakauheni terminal before boarding (20 min). Arrive Merak ~60%. Drive to Jakarta.

Estimated trip cost: Rp 600,000-1,200,000 (ferry return) + Rp 200,000-350,000 (charging) = Rp 800,000-1,550,000 (~$50-100 USD)

Itinerary 2: 10-Day Java-Bali Loop (Surabaya → Ketapang → Gilimanuk → Denpasar → Probolinggo)

The classic Java-Bali road trip, optimised for EVs. This loop takes you from East Java through Bali's highlights and back via the scenic north coast.

Day Route Activities Charging Plan
Day 1 Surabaya → Probolinggo (80 km, 1.5 hrs) Pick up EV in Surabaya, drive south to Probolinggo. Afternoon visit to Madakaripura Waterfall. Charge to 80% at PLN SPKLU Surabaya before departure. Arrive Probolinggo ~60%. Top up at PLN SPKLU Probolinggo (50 kW, 25 min). Hotel AC charging overnight.
Day 2 Probolinggo → Ketapang (100 km, 2 hrs) Morning visit to Mount Bromo viewpoint. Afternoon drive to Banyuwangi. Sunset at Pulau Merah Beach. Charge to 80% in Probolinggo before heading to Bromo (expect 20% extra consumption on mountain roads). Charge at PLN SPKLU Ketapang terminal (50 kW) before ferry dinner or next morning.
Day 3 Ketapang → Gilimanuk → Denpasar Morning ferry to Gilimanuk (30 min). Drive across Bali to Denpasar/Sanur (120 km, 3 hrs). Charge to 70% at Ketapang before boarding. Arrive Gilimanuk ~65%. Charge at new PLN SPKLU Gilimanuk (50 kW, 20 min) then drive east. Or push directly to Denpasar (~120 km, 3 hrs). Top up at PLN SPKLU Sanur or Denpasar on arrival.
Day 4 South Bali Uluwatu temples, Jimbaran seafood, Seminyak shopping Charge at PLN SPKLU Seminyak (50 kW) or resort AC charging overnight.
Day 5 Denpasar → Ubud (40 km, 1 hr) Ubud monkey forest, rice terraces at Tegallalang, Ubud Art Market Hotel AC charging in Ubud. Many Ubud resorts offer free overnight charging.
Day 6 Ubud → Singaraja → Pemuteran (120 km, 3 hrs) Drive north over the mountains to Singaraja. Gitgit Waterfall, Pemuteran beach, Menjangan Island snorkelling Charge to 80% in Ubud before the mountain crossing. The climb over Bali's central mountains uses 20-25% more battery. Resort AC charging in Pemuteran.
Day 7 Pemuteran → Gilimanuk → Ketapang (120 km + ferry) Morning beach time. Afternoon ferry back to Java. Drive to Probolinggo. Charge at PLN SPKLU Gilimanuk (50 kW) before boarding. Top up at PLN SPKLU Probolinggo.
Day 8 Probolinggo → Surabaya (80 km, 1.5 hrs) Return to Surabaya. Mall visit, EV return. Charge at PLN SPKLU Surabaya before returning the EV.

Estimated trip cost: Rp 300,000-700,000 (ferry return) + Rp 400,000-700,000 (charging) = Rp 700,000-1,400,000 (~$45-90 USD) — not including accommodation and activities.

Itinerary 3: 14-Day Sumatra-Java-Bali Grand Tour

The ultimate Indonesian EV road trip — from Sumatra's wild south across Java to Bali's paradise. This is an ambitious trip requiring careful planning and 6-8 DC charging stops.

Day Route Key Charging Stops Notes
Days 1-3 Bandar Lampung → Bakauheni → Merak → Jakarta PLN SPKLU Bandar Lampung (80%), Bakauheni terminal (70%), Merak terminal (70%), Jakarta The Trans-Sumatra Toll Road is well-served with SPKLU stations at rest areas every 50 km south of Bandar Lampung.
Day 4 Jakarta → Semarang (440 km, 6 hrs) PLN SPKLU at rest areas along Trans-Java Toll Road: Cikampek, Cirebon, Pekalongan, Semarang Long drive day. Charge to 80% in Jakarta. Top up at Cirebon (50 kW) mid-way. Charge at Semarang on arrival.
Day 5 Semarang → Surabaya (350 km, 5 hrs) PLN SPKLU at rest areas. Top up at Solo or Ngawi. The Trans-Java Toll Road has SPKLU at nearly every major rest area. Surabaya has multiple charging options.
Days 6-8 Surabaya → Ketapang → Gilimanuk → South Bali As per Itinerary 2. Charge at Ketapang before ferry, Gilimanuk after. See the Java-Bali Loop section above.
Days 9-12 Bali exploration PLN SPKLU Sanur, Seminyak, Gianyar, Ubud Bali has 80+ charging points. Resort AC charging covers most needs.
Day 13 Bali → Padangbai → Lembar → Lombok Charge at Amankila or Gianyar before Padangbai ferry. Charge at PLN SPKLU Mataram or Mandalika on arrival in Lombok. For a detailed Lombok itinerary, see the Bali to Lombok EV Ferry Guide.
Day 14 Lombok exploration or return PLN SPKLU Mandalika, Senggigi, Selong Lombok has 8-10 DC chargers spread across the island.

Practical Tips for Indonesian Ferry Travel with an EV

Booking Ferry Tickets

  • ASDP Ferry app — covers Merak–Bakauheni, Ketapang–Gilimanuk, and Padangbai–Lembar routes. Book 1-7 days in advance for peak periods
  • Kaizen Ferry app — covers some Java-Bali routes with a premium service (faster boarding, better facilities)
  • Peak seasons (Lebaran/Eid, Christmas-New Year, school holidays): book 7-14 days in advance and expect queues of 2-4 hours at terminals
  • Low season: walk-up is usually fine for all routes except Merak–Bakauheni, which is consistently busy
  • EV-specific: When booking via the app, select "Mobil" (car) class. ASDP does not differentiate EV vs petrol pricing

Best Times to Cross

Route Best Times Avoid
Ketapang→Gilimanuk Weekdays 6-9 AM or after 8 PM Saturday mornings, Sunday afternoons, Lebaran week
Merak→Bakauheni Weekdays early morning (4-7 AM) or late night (10 PM-2 AM) Friday evenings (Jakarta weekend exodus), Monday mornings (return), holiday periods
Padangbai→Lembar Weekdays 7-10 AM departures Weekends June-August, MotoGP weekends, Nyepi period

Range Planning: Charge BEFORE the Ferry, Not After

This is the single most important rule: always charge to 70-75% before boarding the ferry. Here's why:

  1. You don't know how long the queue will be — aircon while waiting in terminal traffic can drain 3-5% per hour
  2. The ferry crossing itself drains 5-10% from phantom loads (BMS, tracking, security systems)
  3. The destination terminal's charger might be occupied, broken, or have a queue
  4. If you arrive at the destination with 30% or less, you risk range anxiety immediately after a long trip

The rule of thumb: Arrive at the departure terminal with enough range to reach the nearest DC charger on the other side — plus 30% buffer.

What About Bali's Seasonal Traffic?

Bali has severe traffic during peak tourist season (June-August, December-January). The drive from Gilimanuk to Denpasar/Canggu (120 km) typically takes 2.5-3.5 hours in normal conditions, but can stretch to 5-6 hours during holiday weekends. Factor this into your range planning — heavy traffic with aircon can increase consumption by 10-15%.

What to Do If the Terminal Charger Is Occupied

  • Check PLN Mobile app for other nearby SPKLU stations — PLN shows real-time availability
  • Use the ChargeIN app as a backup — covers Bali and some Java chargers
  • Head to a nearby hotel — many hotels in Indonesia will let you use their wall box (even if not a guest) for a small fee (Rp 50,000-100,000)
  • Use a granny charger at a terminal warung (small restaurant) — ask nicely, offer Rp 20,000-50,000 for the electricity
  • Join the local EV queue — EV drivers in Indonesia are a friendly community and will often share real-time updates on which chargers are free

Cost Comparison: EV vs Petrol for Inter-Island Travel

Scenario EV Charging Cost Petrol Cost Savings with EV
3-day Java Explorer (350 km driving) Rp 200,000-350,000 Rp 450,000-650,000 Rp 200,000-300,000
10-day Java-Bali Loop (1,000 km driving) Rp 400,000-700,000 Rp 1,200,000-1,800,000 Rp 600,000-1,100,000
14-day Grand Tour (2,500 km driving) Rp 1,000,000-1,500,000 Rp 3,000,000-4,500,000 Rp 2,000,000-3,000,000

Note: DC charging in Indonesia costs approximately Rp 2,467/kWh at PLN SPKLU stations. A typical 60 kWh EV charging from 20% to 80% (36 kWh) costs roughly Rp 89,000 ($5.70). Hotel AC charging is often free for guests.

The EV advantage is most pronounced on longer trips with more driving — the 10-day Java-Bali Loop saves Rp 600,000-1,100,000 (~$40-70 USD) just on energy costs. Ferry costs are identical between EV and petrol vehicles.

Future Outlook: Indonesia's 2026 SPKLU Expansion and New RORO Routes

SPKLU Expansion at Ports

PLN's 2026 SPKLU expansion includes several key port-area deployments:

  • Gilimanuk (Bali) — 2x 50 kW SPKLU installed early 2026 ✅ (active)
  • Ketapang (Java) — 1x 50 kW existing, 1x additional planned late 2026
  • Merak (Java) — Expansion to 4x 50 kW and 2x 100 kW planned Q3 2026
  • Bakauheni (Sumatra) — Expanding from 3x to 6x units with new 100 kW chargers by Q4 2026
  • Padangbai (Bali) — PLN has announced plans for an on-terminal SPKLU by end of 2026
  • Lembar (Lombok) — Discussions for terminal charging in 2027

New RORO Routes in Development

  • Bali → Nusa Penida — Car ferry service expanding (currently passenger-only fast boats). No timeline yet, but Nusa Penida is a popular tourist destination
  • Sumatra → Malaysia (Dumai–Malacca) — Cross-border RORO service that could connect Indonesia's Sumatra charging network with Malaysia's. Early feasibility studies underway
  • Java → Kalimantan (Surabaya–Banjarmasin) — Long-distance RORO service being explored by the Ministry of Transportation. Would open up Borneo to island-hopping EV travellers
  • Eastern Indonesia expansion — Makassar (Sulawesi) to Manado, Ambon, and Jayapura routes being studied for the ASEAN EV ecosystem

Charging Network Growth on Key Islands

Island Current DC Chargers (June 2026) Target (End 2026) Notes
Java 450+ 600+ Best coverage in ASEAN — Trans-Java Toll Road is fully covered
Bali 80+ 120+ Concentrated in south coast and Ubud
Sumatra 60+ 120+ Growing fast — Trans-Sumatra Toll Road being electrified
Lombok 8-10 15+ Mandalika area leads, expanding to north and east
Sulawesi 15+ 30+ Makassar and Manado hubs, limited coverage elsewhere

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I take any EV on an Indonesian RORO ferry?

Yes. ASDP and Kaizen Ferry accept all standard electric vehicles at normal vehicle rates. Standard EVs (Tesla Model Y, BYD Atto 3, Hyundai Ioniq 5, Wuling Air EV, Honda N-Van EV) fit easily. Oversized vehicles (4x4s with roof racks, Hummer EV) may need to check height/width limits — most ferry decks have 2.5m clearance.

Do I need to book the ferry in advance for an EV?

During peak seasons (Lebaran, Christmas-New Year, school holidays), yes — book 7-14 days ahead through the ASDP app. Off-peak, same-day walk-up is usually fine for Ketapang-Gilimanuk and Padangbai-Lembar. Merak-Bakauheni is consistently busy — book 3-7 days ahead even off-peak.

Is it safe to take my EV on an Indonesian ferry crossing?

Yes. Modern EV batteries are sealed and waterproof. The Sunda Strait and Lombok Strait are sheltered waters (not open ocean), and the ferry decks are covered. Your EV will be fine. The only precaution: ensure proper chocking and follow crew instructions for parking brake (some crews prefer it released on the deck for stacking).

Can I charge at the ferry terminals?

For most major terminals, yes — but check the status before you go:

  • Merak: ✅ Yes — 2x 50 kW DC + 4x AC
  • Bakauheni: ✅ Yes — 3x 50 kW DC + additional SPKLU
  • Ketapang: ✅ Yes — 1x 50 kW DC
  • Gilimanuk: ✅ Yes — 2x 50 kW DC (NEW — early 2026)
  • Padangbai: ❌ No — nearest DC is 20 km north at Amankila
  • Lembar: ❌ No — nearest DC is 30 km north at Mataram

What happens if there's a queue at the terminal charger?

Plan ahead. Use the PLN Mobile app to check charger availability. Have a backup plan: either arrive early, charge at a nearby town before approaching the terminal, or bring a granny charger for emergency use. The new Gilimanuk chargers (installed early 2026) have significantly reduced congestion at the Bali side.

What's the easiest first-time Indonesian EV ferry route?

Ketapang (Banyuwangi) → Gilimanuk (Bali) is the easiest — it's a 30-minute crossing with ferries every 15 minutes, charging at both terminals, and Bali has excellent charging infrastructure on arrival. Perfect for a first inter-island EV trip from Surabaya or East Java.

Is Lombok's charging network sufficient for an EV?

For a 3-5 day trip, yes — if you plan around Lombok's 8-10 public DC chargers and use hotel AC charging overnight. The network is strategically placed around the tourist circuit (Mataram → Senggigi → Mandalika). For full details, see our dedicated Bali to Lombok EV Ferry Guide.

Can I drive an EV from Jakarta to Bali?

Absolutely. Take the Trans-Java Toll Road from Jakarta to Surabaya (780 km, fully electrified with SPKLU stations at every major rest area), then continue east to Ketapang (Banyuwangi) for the 30-minute ferry to Gilimanuk, Bali. The full Jakarta-to-Denpasar drive is approximately 1,000 km plus the ferry. Plan for 3-4 days of driving with charging stops every 2-3 hours.

What's the best charging app for Indonesian inter-island travel?

PLN Mobile is the most essential app — it covers all SPKLU stations operated by PLN, which is the vast majority of public DC fast chargers in Indonesia. As a backup, ChargeIN covers many Bali chargers and some Java stations. For ferry booking, use the ASDP Ferry app. For real-time charger availability from the community, join the "EV Indonesia" Telegram group.

The Bottom Line

Inter-island EV travel in Indonesia is not just possible — it's becoming genuinely practical in 2026. The three major RORO routes (Ketapang–Gilimanuk, Merak–Bakauheni, and Padangbai–Lembar) all have functional charging ecosystems on both sides, with new SPKLU installations at Gilimanuk and Bakauheni making the experience significantly smoother than even 12 months ago.

Key takeaways:

  • Java → Bali (Ketapang–Gilimanuk) is the easiest route — 30 min crossing, charging at both terminals, ferries every 15 minutes. Start here for your first trip.
  • Java → Sumatra (Merak–Bakauheni) requires the most planning — longer crossing, consistent crowds, but excellent terminal charging on both sides.
  • Bali → Lombok (Padangbai–Lembar) is the most adventurous — 3-4 hour crossing, no terminal charging yet, but Lombok's strategic 8-10 DC points make it workable.
  • Charge to 70-75% before every ferry — this is the single most important rule. Phantom drain plus uncertainty at the destination makes full-battery departures essential.
  • Bring a Type 2 cable and a granny charger — hotel AC charging and emergency wall socket access are your backup lifelines.
  • PLN's 2026 expansion is changing the game — new chargers at Gilimanuk, upgrades at Merak and Bakauheni, and planned installations at Padangbai mean the network is getting better every quarter.

Indonesia is uniquely suited to EV island-hopping. The distances between islands are short, the ferry network is extensive, and the charging infrastructure — while still concentrated on the Java-Bali-Sumatra corridor — is expanding rapidly. A well-planned EV road trip across Indonesia's islands is one of the most rewarding driving experiences in Southeast Asia, combining world-class scenery with the quiet, emissions-free joy of electric driving.

Ready to take your EV across Indonesian islands? Use our EV charger map to plan your charging stops at every terminal, toll rest area, and city along your route.

Charging prices, ferry schedules, and SPKLU availability as of June 2026. Always verify current rates on the PLN Mobile app and check the ASDP Ferry app for real-time ferry schedules and booking. Ferry terminal charging infrastructure is subject to maintenance and peak-season demand — have a backup plan. New SPKLU installations at Gilimanuk (installed early 2026) and planned expansions at Merak, Bakauheni, and Padangbai are part of PLN's nationwide charging network development.
